{{Short description|Convex polyhedron property}}
In mathematics, a [[convex polyhedron]] is defined to be <math>k</math>-'''equiprojective''' if every [[orthogonal projection]] of the polygon onto a plane, in a direction not parallel to a face of the polyhedron, forms a <math>k</math>-gon. For example, a [[cube]] is 6-equiprojective: every projection not parallel to a face forms a [[hexagon]], More generally, every [[Prism (geometry)|prism]] over a convex <math>k</math> is <math>(k+2)</math>-equiprojective.{{r|shephard|cfg}} [[Zonohedron|Zonohedra]] are also equiprojective.{{r|buffiere}} Hasan and his colleagues later found more equiprojective polyhedra by truncating equally the tetrahedron and three other [[Johnson solid]]s.{{r|hhl}}

{{harvtxt|Hasan|Lubiw|2008}} shows there is an <math> O(n \log n) </math> time algorithm to determine whether a given polyhedron is equiprojective.{{r|hl}}
